title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). k is a commutative ring, often noetherian. 'Un k-module ½ simplicial L.' is a simplicial k-module. L^! is its Dold–Puppe (normalized Moore) chain complex. L is called ∂-pseudo-coherent, ∂-perfect, etc. when L^! has the corresponding property.

The key structural fact behind the page is the Dold–Kan splitting L_n ≅ ⊕_{[n]↠[i]} L^!_i. Since there are C(n,i) surjections [n]↠[i], this gives L_n ≅ ⊕_i L^!_i^{⊕C(n,i)}.

The basic objects of Prop. 1(c) are Λ^i E ⊗ M_i, with E presumably the simplicial module with E_n = Z^n, i.e. K(Z,1). Then Λ^i E has rank C(n,i) in degree n. Its normalized complex is free of rank one in degree i, so Λ^i E ≅ K(Z,i).

This page finishes Prop. 1(e). Hypotheses: k noetherian regular, L_n of finite type. Claim: L is ∂-perfect iff, for every x ∈ Spec k, the function n ↦ rg_{k(x)} L_n ⊗ k(x) is polynomial for n large. Grothendieck adds:
- the degree of the polynomial is the largest i with L^!_i ⊗ k(x) ≠ 0;
- in the binomial basis P_i(n) = C(n,i), the coefficients are rg_{k(x)} L^!_i ⊗ k(x);
- these coefficients are constructible functions of x ∈ Spec k, 'up to the usual exception at the beginning'.
All of this is immediate from the Dold–Kan splitting by tensoring with k(x).

NB (non-regular k). The naive criterion is then 'doubtless necessary but not sufficient'. The correct criterion is that there exist L' → L with L' strictly ∂-perfect (see (c)) inducing isomorphisms on all π_i. One may moreover take L' → L to be an epimorphism. This is the definition of perfection (quasi-isomorphic to a strictly perfect complex), transported through Dold–Kan; surjectivity is obtained by adding a contractible summand.

Grothendieck then announces his aim: a 'théorie de la stabilité' for strictly ∂-perfect L. He notes this is only possible for a class of objects more stable than ∂-perfect ones (the reading here is uncertain). A margin note begins 'Stabilité des …'.

The next page carries out the programme over a principal (Dedekind) ring. It gives an isomorphism (not homotopy) classification of ∂-pseudo-coherent simplicial modules as products of three kinds of building block: M_i ⊗ Λ^iΦ, N_j ⊗ Λ^jΨ, and Φ(i,ℓ), the last indexed by divisors ℓ. This is the simplicial analogue of decomposing a complex of free modules over a PID into elementary complexes.

Purpose: a dévissage of simplicial modules into elementary pieces, presumably in preparation for multiplicative structures (the title).
errors: As stated, the polynomial-rank criterion characterises L^! having finitely generated components that vanish in large degrees. It does not characterise perfection up to quasi-isomorphism.

A ∂-perfect L in the non-strict sense can have L^! nonzero in arbitrarily high degrees, for instance with a contractible tail. So the criterion is neither necessary for ∂-perfection nor 'doubtless necessary' in the non-regular case, unless one reads 'strictly' or works up to homotopy.

Over regular k, sufficiency holds: a bounded complex of finitely generated modules over a regular noetherian ring is perfect. The correct statement is therefore 'L is homotopy equivalent to such an L', or a statement about the strict version.
The 'exception habituelle au commencement' is unnecessary when L^! is bounded. In the basis C(n,i) the rank formula is exactly polynomial for all n ≥ 0.

Constructibility of the coefficients x ↦ rg L^!_i ⊗ k(x) is standard: fibre ranks of finitely generated modules over a noetherian ring are constructible (indeed upper semicontinuous). Grothendieck asserts it without proof, which is fine.

ideas.what: Fibre ranks of L_n are polynomial in n, with binomial coefficients equal to the fibre ranks of the normalized complex: rg L_n = Σ_i C(n,i)·rg L^!_i.
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan splitting L_n ≅ ⊕_{[n]↠[i]} N_i; rank generating function of a simplicial module

ideas.what: Constructibility in x ∈ Spec k of the fibre ranks of the normalized components.
ideas.where_published: EGA IV (constructibility); SGA 6 (pseudo-coherent and perfect complexes)

ideas.what: Over non-regular k, perfection is characterised by a quasi-isomorphism (which may be chosen surjective) from a strictly perfect simplicial module.
ideas.modern_name: Perfect complex = locally quasi-isomorphic to a strictly perfect complex, transported by Dold–Kan

ideas.what: Programme: a 'stability theory' / dévissage for strictly ∂-perfect simplicial modules, leading on the next page to an isomorphism classification over PIDs by building blocks Λ^iΦ, Λ^jΨ, Φ(i,ℓ).
ideas.modern_name: Structure theory of simplicial modules up to isomorphism (not homotopy) over Dedekind rings; analogue of elementary-divisor decomposition of complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; no standard reference known to me

missed.claim: Grothendieck announces a 'théorie de la stabilité' for strictly ∂-perfect simplicial modules. This seems to mean classification or rigidity up to isomorphism rather than homotopy, possibly behaviour under base change. He sketches it only over principal rings on the next page. The notion is neither defined nor developed here.
missed.quote: On veut une théorie de la stab. pour des L str. ∂-parfaits
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Classifying simplicial modules up to strict isomorphism, not up to homotopy, is rarely studied. A genuine structure theory over Dedekind rings could matter for explicit models (e.g. Λ^i K(Z,1)) used in multiplicative and derived-functor computations. The significance is modest and the thread too fragmentary to evaluate.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is essentially a routine consequence of the Dold–Kan splitting: binomial rank polynomial and constructible coefficients. It also restates the standard SGA 6 characterisation of perfect complexes. The only open element is a one-line announcement of a 'stability theory', developed (over PIDs) on the next page, not here.
transcription_corrections: 'rg_k L_n ⊗_k k' should read 'rg_{k(x)} L_n ⊗_k k(x)', the rank of the fibre at the residue field of x ∈ Spec k.
'L^i_n ≠ 0' and 'rg_k L^i_n ⊗_k k' should read 'L^!_i ≠ 0' and 'rg L^!_i ⊗ k(x)', i.e. components of the normalized complex.
'(composantes non nulles, i.e. L_i ≠ 0)' likely refers to L^!_i ⊗ k(x) ≠ 0.
'fonctions constructibles en le point variable [?] ∈ Spec k' should read '… le point variable x ∈ Spec k'.
'NB Si dans ce [?] espace [?] de [?] mais non régulier' is probably 'NB Si dans e) k est noethérien mais non régulier'.
'qui soit un [?] i.e. induise un iso sur les π_i' is probably 'qui soit un quasi-iso (quis), i.e. …'.
'DPS L' → L épi' is probably 'on peut supposer L' → L épi'.
